correctness.rationale: For the exact diagonal rate update, put A=τρ. Both updated coordinates are nonnegative for all positive τ,ρ and all simplex inputs. The gain in the residual is (s−s_+)−(i_+−i)=τi[1+As(1−ρi)/(1+Ai)]/(1+τ). At fixed i the residual itself is affine in s with coefficient −1/(1+Ai)−Ai/(1+τ)<0. Thus the worst input has s=1−i and r=0, and its residual is τi[1+A−Aρi(1−i)]/[(1+τ)(1+Ai)]. The i=0 value is zero; the quadratic factor is minimized at i=1/2, so the condition τρ(ρ−4)≤4 is necessary and sufficient and includes equality. Solving the strict quadratic gives the two stated infected-fraction roots; solving the affine residual inequality gives s_*(i), with a nonempty unsafe interval at fixed i exactly between those roots. Substituting τ=γh and ρ=βN/γ gives the stated h threshold. At (ρ,τ)=(5,1), the half-half input gives −1/56; at (5,4/5) it gives zero. Iteration of a simplex self-map then proves the all-step consequence, not a trajectory-specific claim when the criterion fails. RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected without running the uploaded code. RESULT.md overdescribes the checker as comparing polynomial coefficients: the frozen script does exact rational substitution on grids and witnesses instead. This is a reproducibility-description error, not a missing proof; the algebra above verifies the identity for arbitrary inputs. The claim does not extend to fitted rates or floating-point equality.

value.rationale: The originating work explicitly flags negative reconstructed R; a numerical analyst deciding whether to use this splitting needs a guarantee for the whole simplex, not just independent positivity of S and I. The result gives the exact unrestricted range, a sharp denominator or step bound outside it, and a certified geometry of failure. It also separates numerical infeasibility from the usual continuous-time epidemic threshold and from behavior of learned rates.
